n only\nruns when no explicit CLI target overrides the file. Environment attachment\nsynchronization is unaffected and always runs

.

Without `--idempotency-key`, the CLI mints a fresh UUID for every invocation
and prints it to stderr before launch (`Eval id
empotency key: <key>`). Each\ninvocation therefore starts and bills a new run. To retry a launch whose\nresponse was lost (without
starting a second run), pass the key that was\nprinted: `--idempotency-key <printed-key>`. A replay is marked `deduped` in\nthe r

eceipt and human output. `--notes` is not part of the key.

##### Imported cases: live tool resolution, and per-run approval
Every file run performs the same live check `eval validate --project` performs,\n**before it writes anything**. It is not opt-in a

nd there is no flag to skip
it. A file with no deterministic `toolCall` steps asks no question and pays no
round trip.

What h

appens when a deterministic reference does not resolve depends on the
case:

| Case | Outcome |
| - | - |
| Selected (enabled
, and named by `--case` if you used it) | The launch **refuses before the suite is synced**: nothing is written and nothing is bil
led |\n| Imported, not selected | Its claim is rewritten to `unresolved` (keeping `sourceCaseKey`) and it is **still persisted**,
so the hosted record says what MCPJam found rather than still asserting a claim about a missing tool |\n| Native, not selected | L
eft exactly as authored. A hand-written case never acquires an `import` block from this: \"somebody wrote this\" and \"something c

onverted this" are different facts |

Each target is checked on **its own** server set. `--host` is checked against
that host'
s configured servers rather than the file's, because that is the set\nthe run connects: validating `target.servers` would approve
a tool the host\ncannot reach. A host the FILE declares uses its own `servers` list when it\ndeclares one (those are attached to t
he host before launch) and the host's\nconfigured set when the field is omitted. An explicitly empty `servers: []`\nis a real, emp
ty set (it clears the attachment before launch) and is\nvalidated as such, never as an omitted field. A step that pins `serverId`
ore the suite exists\n(`--all-targets`, `--compose-*`), or a host does not report a server set, or a\nhost pins a server the proje

ct no longer has, the launch refuses rather than
assuming the references are fine.

`--case` accepts a hosted row id, which doe
s not exist yet when this check\nruns. A selector this stage cannot map is therefore treated as possibly naming\nany enabled case,

so an unresolved reference still refuses; the launcher
resolves the selector itself a moment later.

A selected `approximated`

case refuses unless this invocation approves it:

| Flag | Required | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `--allow-approximated <ca
se...>` | No | Approve an `approximated` imported case for **this run only**, by AUTHORED case id (`cases[].id`). Repeatable. `--f
ile` runs only |\n| `--approval-reason <text>` | With the above | Why the approximations are acceptable for this run. 1–500 charac
loud eval run --file .mcpjam/evals/s_billing.yaml \\\n --allow-approximated c_refund_partial \\\n --approval-reason \"Reviewed a

gainst the upstream rubric; ENG-4821"
```

Checked before anything is billed, each with its own message: approving a
**native
** case (nothing to approve), a **claimed-exact** one (needs no\napproval), an **unsupported** or **unresolved** one (approval cov
ers a case\nwhose behaviour was approximated, not one whose behaviour is missing), a\n**disabled** or **unselected** one (the run
will not execute it), an unknown\nid, or the same id twice. The flags are refused outright with `--suite`: a\nhosted suite's cases

are not the ones this invocation authored, so an
authored-id selector has nothing to resolve against.

**The approval belongs
to the run, never to the case.** You supply an id and a\nreason and nothing else; the approver and the timestamp are derived by th
e\nserver and frozen into that run's own snapshot, because a caller-supplied\napprover would file one person's approval under anot
her's name and a\ncaller-supplied timestamp could be backdated past the edit that invalidated the\nclaim. Nothing persists: edit t

he suite, re-sync, or launch again, and the flags
are required again.

Scheduled runs cannot approve anything. A scheduled suit
e\ncontaining a selected approximation is refused by platform policy, which is the\nintended behaviour; an unattended job is exact

ly the caller that must not be
able to wave one through.

`--file` pointing at create-API JSON (no `schemaVersion`) is a usage
error\nthat names `eval create --file`. The converse is also true: `eval create --file`\non a versioned suite file names `eval run

--file`.

Export of a file-owned suite writes `declaredId` as `suite.id`. Export of a
UI-owned suite derives a stable file ide

ntity (`s_export_<sourceSuiteId>`),

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--project <id-or-name>` | Project name or ID (default
s to the most recently updated project) |\n| `--all-projects` | List across every accessible project. Conflicts with `--project`.

|
| `--status <status>` | Filter by session status |
| `--limit <n>` | Maximum sessions to return (1–200) |

### `cloud sessio
ns send`\n\nSend one message to a project's MCP servers and print the reply plus the raw tool calls, per-call latency and token us

age: the telemetry a participant in the conversation cannot see.

**This spends model credits on every call.**

`--idempotency
-key` is required and must be **stable for the intent**, not regenerated per attempt. It is what makes a retry safe: with the same
key, a turn that already completed is replayed rather than re-run and re-billed. A fresh key per attempt deduplicates nothing.\n\
nOmit `--session` to start a conversation; pass the `sessionId` the command returns to continue one. After the first model turn, t
he session is configured: `--model`, `--environment`, `--server`, `--no-servers`, `--system-prompt` and `--tool-mode` are then ref

used alongside `--session` rather than silently repinning it.

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--message <text>` | The mes
sage to send, as the user (required) |\n| `--idempotency-key <key>` | Stable key for this turn's intent (required). Reuse it when
retrying. |\n| `--session <sessionId>` | Continue this session instead of starting one |\n| `--model <modelId>` | Provider-prefixe
d model id, e.g. `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`. Optional on the first send: defaults to the selected environment’s or client’s model
and is then pinned. A supplied ID must be provider-prefixed. |\n| `--environment <environmentId>` | Target this environment's ser
vers. Conflicts with `--server`. |\n| `--server <serverId...>` | Target these project servers. Conflicts with `--environment`. |\n
| `--no-servers` | Start with no MCP servers. Conflicts with `--server` and `--environment`; requires a deployment with chat-envir
onment support. |\n| `--system-prompt <text>` | System prompt for the session |\n| `--tool-mode <mode>` | `read_only` (default) ad
vertises only tools annotated `readOnlyHint: true`. `auto` advertises everything and **may cause real side effects**. |\n| `--max-
steps <n>` | Maximum engine steps this turn (1–16) |\n| `--max-tool-calls <n>` | Cap the tool calls this turn may make. `0` answer
s without tools. |\n| `--temperature <n>` | Sampling temperature (0–2) |\n| `--effort <level>` | Reasoning effort for the model. F
irst turn only: pinned to the session, refused with `--session`. It replaces the temperature, so it cannot be combined with `--tem
perature`. Applied or refused by the rail the model runs on, never dropped |\n| `--project <id-or-name>` | Project name or ID (req
uired to start a session) |\n\n`read_only` filters on a hint the SERVER asserts, so it is a policy this host applies rather than a

guarantee it can verify. A server is free to annotate a mutating tool as read-only.
